previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson, a male with a history of mixed Hodgkin's and non-Hodgkin's lymphoma with CNS involvement, was admitted for maintenance high-dose methotrexate and rituximab chemotherapy. He remained asymptomatic throughout the stay but developed transient acute kidney injury with creatinine peaking at 1.9 mg/dL, likely methotrexate-induced, which improved to 1.5 mg/dL by discharge. Leucovorin was increased to 100 mg every six hours during the period of renal dysfunction. Mild transaminitis and hypokalemia were noted and managed supportively. Constipation was treated with a Fleet's enema and transition to Miralax. Omeprazole and aspirin were held during admission and restarted at discharge. Methotrexate levels declined appropriately, falling below 0.1 µM by discharge. He was discharged home in stable condition with plans for outpatient MRI and ophthalmology follow-up.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ man with CNS lymphoma receiving high dose methotrexate
with severe acute onset headache and nausea.  Evaluate for hemorrhage,
evidence of intracranial hypertension.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial MDCT images of the brain were obtained without
the administration of IV contrast.  Reformatted coronal and sagittal and
thin-section bone algorithm reconstructed images were obtained.

COMPARISON:  MR ___ from ___.

FINDINGS:

There is no evidence of acute hemorrhage, mass effect, edema or acute major
vascular territorial infarction.  The ventricles are asymmetric in size, left
larger than right, unchanged. Foci of low density in the deep and
periventricular white matter on the left are also unchanged compared to the
prior MRI, allowing for differences in modalities; these may be related to the
sequela of CNS lymphoma or chronic small vessel ischemic disease.  The basilar
cisterns appear patent.  

There is minimal mucosal thickening seen within the left inferior frontal
sinus, bilateral ethmoid air cells and left maxillary sinus.  The mastoids are
underpneumatized, with only the mastoid antrum pneumatized on the left, and
small number of pneumatized air cells on the right. No mastoid opacification
is seen. 

IMPRESSION:

Stable appearance of the brain without evidence of an acute intracranial
abnormality.

HISTORY:  ___ year old man with Hodgkins lymphoma on methotrexate with left
upper extremity swelling 

COMPARISON:  None.  

FINDINGS:

Grayscale, color, and spectral Doppler evaluation was performed of the left
upper extremity veins.  

There is normal phasicity of the subclavian veins bilaterally.  There is
normal compression and augmentation of the left internal jugular, axillary,
paired brachial, basilic, and cephalic veins.  

IMPRESSION:

No evidence of DVT in the left upper extremity.
